title: Only 7% Pass This Car Mechanic Quiz
summary: Warning lights, engine faults, brakes, fluids and road symptoms get harder across 10 workshop rounds.

landing.intro: From warning lights to strange noises, prove you can find the fault before the repair bill arrives.

about.body:
This practical car mechanic quiz turns dashboard warnings, vehicle systems and everyday fault symptoms into ten increasingly difficult workshop rounds. Questions cover engines and fuel, braking and road grip, electrical starting systems, cooling and fluids, drivetrain and steering, diagnosis and essential vehicle safety.

The challenge is designed for curious car owners and enthusiasts who enjoy automotive knowledge, maintenance basics and diagnostic problem-solving. Some questions test familiar warning signs, while others ask you to follow a component sequence, compare two symptoms or identify the safest next step without carrying out a repair.

Your final score reflects only the answers selected in this entertainment quiz. Vehicles and procedures differ, so the result is a playful snapshot of the systems you recognised most confidently rather than proof of professional competence.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer six questions in each workshop round and choose the single option you think is best.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so diagnose each clue before the quiz moves on.
Complete all ten rounds to reveal your Mechanic Score, strongest system and trickiest area.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a professional qualification or vehicle-repair diagnosis. Vehicles differ; consult the manufacturer’s guidance and a qualified technician.

questions.question: Which warning symbol most directly relates to engine oil pressure?
questions.explanation: The oil-can symbol warns of an engine oil-pressure problem, which can quickly damage the engine.

questions.question: A red brake warning stays on after the parking brake is released. What is the safest response?
answers: Stop safely and have the brake system checked
Ignore it until the next service
questions.explanation: A persistent red brake warning may indicate a serious hydraulic or braking fault and should be checked before continuing.

questions.question: The starter produces one solid click but does not turn the engine. Which is the most useful first check?
questions.explanation: A weak battery or poor terminal connection commonly causes a click without enough current to crank the engine.

questions.question: The temperature warning turns red while driving. What should you do?
answers: Pour cold water on the engine
Stop safely, switch off and let the system cool
questions.explanation: Stopping and allowing the system to cool reduces damage and burn risk; a hot pressurised cap must not be opened.

questions.question: Which control changes the direction of the front wheels?
questions.explanation: The steering wheel operates the steering system, which changes the angle of the road wheels.

questions.question: Before inspecting any unfamiliar fault, what should come first?
answers: Making the vehicle and work area safe
questions.explanation: Securing the vehicle and identifying hazards must come before diagnosis or repair.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes air entering a typical combustion engine?

visual.ariaLabel: Air inlet, filter, intake system, engine

questions.explanation: Incoming air normally travels through the inlet and filter, through the intake system and into the engine.

questions.question: Which part cleans dust from the air before it reaches the engine?
questions.explanation: The air filter traps dust and debris before intake air enters the engine.

questions.question: Which component produces electrical power while a conventional engine is running?
questions.explanation: The alternator supplies electrical power and recharges the 12-volt battery while the engine runs.

questions.question: Where is engine coolant normally checked when the engine is cold?
questions.explanation: The marked coolant expansion reservoir provides a safe level check when the system is cold.

questions.question: What is the radiator’s main job?
answers: Transfer heat from coolant to the air
questions.explanation: The radiator removes heat from circulating coolant by transferring it to passing air.

questions.question: You find an unidentified puddle under a parked car. What is the best first step?
answers: Drive until the level warning appears
Note its location and colour without touching it
questions.explanation: Location and appearance provide useful clues without the danger of tasting or directly handling an unknown automotive fluid.

questions.question: Which fluid primarily lubricates moving parts inside the engine?
questions.explanation: Engine oil forms a lubricating film between moving internal components and also helps carry away heat.

questions.question: Why must a hot pressurised cooling-system cap remain closed?
answers: Escaping hot coolant and steam can cause severe burns
questions.explanation: Releasing a hot pressurised cooling system can suddenly eject boiling coolant and steam.

questions.question: The coolant level keeps falling but no puddle is visible. What does that suggest?
answers: A leak may occur only when hot or internally
questions.explanation: Some leaks appear only under heat and pressure, while internal leaks may leave no external puddle.

questions.question: Brake fluid has dropped below its marked minimum. What is the correct response?
answers: Ignore it if braking feels normal
Have the braking system inspected for wear or leakage
questions.explanation: A low brake-fluid level can reflect worn pads or a hydraulic leak and needs proper inspection.

questions.question: Thick black smoke from a combustion engine usually suggests what?
answers: Too much fuel or too little air
questions.explanation: Black exhaust smoke commonly indicates an overly rich mixture caused by excess fuel or restricted air.

questions.question: Brake fluid can damage paint. What should happen after a spill?
answers: Follow the manufacturer’s safe clean-up guidance immediately
questions.explanation: Brake fluid can attack painted surfaces, so prompt, appropriate clean-up is important.

questions.question: A high-pitched squeal appears whenever the brakes are applied. What is the most likely first area to inspect?
questions.explanation: Brake-pad wear indicators or pad vibration commonly produce a repeatable squeal during braking.

questions.question: The brake pedal feels soft and sinks unusually far. What should you suspect?
answers: Air or a leak in the hydraulic brake system
questions.explanation: A soft or sinking pedal points toward hydraulic pressure loss, often from air or leakage.

questions.question: What does ABS help a driver retain during hard braking?
questions.explanation: ABS limits sustained wheel lock so the tyres can retain more steering ability under hard braking.

questions.question: Why is correct tyre pressure important?
answers: It supports grip, stability and even tyre wear
questions.explanation: Correct pressure helps the tyre maintain its intended contact patch, handling and wear pattern.

questions.question: A rhythmic clicking becomes faster on tight turns. Which part is a likely cause?
questions.explanation: A worn outer constant-velocity joint commonly clicks in rhythm with wheel speed on turns.

questions.question: One tyre has a deep sidewall bulge. What should you do?
answers: Stop using the tyre and arrange replacement
questions.explanation: A sidewall bulge indicates structural damage and a risk of sudden tyre failure.

questions.question: A combustion engine needs which basic combination to run?

visual.ariaLabel: Air plus fuel plus ignition plus compression

answers: Air, fuel, compression and correctly timed ignition
Oil, steering angle and tyre pressure
questions.explanation: A combustion engine needs the correct air-fuel mixture, compression and a correctly timed ignition event.

questions.question: A blocked air filter is most likely to cause what?
answers: Restricted airflow and reduced engine performance
questions.explanation: A clogged filter restricts intake airflow, which can reduce performance and disturb the fuel mixture.

questions.question: One cylinder misfires and its spark plug is badly worn. What is the most direct link?
answers: The plug may fail to ignite the mixture reliably
questions.explanation: A worn spark plug may produce a weak or inconsistent spark, causing that cylinder to misfire.

questions.question: A fuel injector’s basic job is to do what?
questions.explanation: An injector precisely meters fuel into the intake or combustion chamber.

questions.question: The engine overheats in traffic but cools at road speed. Which component deserves an early check?
questions.explanation: Road speed forces air through the radiator; overheating only at low speed strongly points toward missing fan airflow.

questions.question: Which sensor commonly tells the engine computer how much air is entering?
questions.explanation: An airflow sensor measures incoming air so the engine computer can calculate appropriate fuelling.

questions.question: A healthy 12-volt battery reads about 12.6 V at rest. This one reads 10.5 V. What does that suggest?

visual.ariaLabel: Expected battery voltage 12.6 volts, measured 10.5 volts

answers: The battery is deeply discharged or has a failed cell
questions.explanation: A resting voltage near 10.5 V often indicates a severely discharged battery or one failed internal cell.

questions.question: A fuse blows again immediately after replacement. What should happen next?
answers: Find the short or overload before using the circuit
questions.explanation: Repeated fuse failure means the protected circuit still has an overload or short that must be diagnosed.

questions.question: The lights brighten when the engine starts. Why?
answers: The charging system raises system voltage
questions.explanation: Once running, the charging system normally raises voltage above the battery’s resting level.

questions.question: Which component protects a wire from excessive current?
questions.explanation: A correctly rated fuse opens the circuit when current exceeds a safe level.

questions.question: The engine cranks normally but will not start. Which clue makes a starter-motor fault least likely?
answers: The engine is already turning at normal cranking speed
questions.explanation: If the starter is already cranking the engine normally, the no-start fault lies elsewhere in fuel, ignition, control or compression.

questions.question: Before probing an unfamiliar electrical connector, what is safest?
answers: Consult correct service information and use suitable test equipment
questions.explanation: Incorrect probing can damage electronics or trigger safety systems, so correct information and equipment are essential.

questions.question: The steering wheel vibrates mainly at one road-speed range. What is a likely first suspect?
questions.explanation: Wheel imbalance commonly creates a speed-dependent vibration felt through the steering wheel.

questions.question: The car pulls to one side on a level road. Which area should be checked?
questions.explanation: Unequal tyre pressure, alignment faults and related steering issues can cause a steady pull.

questions.question: Engine speed rises sharply but road speed barely increases. What is likely slipping?
questions.explanation: Rising engine speed without matching acceleration indicates power is not being transmitted effectively.

questions.question: A low humming grows louder with road speed, even in neutral. Which component is a likely source?
questions.explanation: A worn wheel bearing often produces a hum or growl tied to road speed rather than engine speed.

questions.question: The whole car shakes only when braking from higher speed. What is a common cause?
questions.explanation: Uneven brake-disc surfaces can create a repeating brake-force variation and vibration under braking.

questions.question: A new severe vibration appears after striking a road hazard. What should you do?
answers: Increase speed to smooth it out
Stop safely and inspect the wheel and tyre before continuing
Ignore it if no warning appears
questions.explanation: A sudden vibration after impact may indicate dangerous wheel, tyre or suspension damage.

questions.question: An orange high-voltage cable is damaged. What should you do?
answers: Avoid touching it and get qualified help
questions.explanation: Orange cabling commonly identifies a high-voltage vehicle system and must only be handled by appropriately trained professionals.

questions.question: Which part grips a brake disc?
questions.explanation: Brake pads clamp against the rotating brake disc to create friction.

questions.question: What recharges the 12-volt battery while driving?
questions.explanation: The vehicle’s charging system supplies electrical energy and maintains the 12-volt battery.

questions.question: Which fluid prevents freezing and carries engine heat?
questions.explanation: Correct coolant provides freeze protection and transports heat through the cooling system.

questions.question: Which joint transmits drive while a wheel steers?
questions.explanation: A constant-velocity joint transmits drive while accommodating steering and suspension movement.

questions.question: You smell fuel. What comes first?
answers: Stop safely, avoid ignition sources and get help
questions.explanation: Fuel vapour can ignite, so stop safely, remove ignition risks and seek qualified assistance.

questions.question: “The car pulls left only while braking, and the left front wheel becomes unusually hot.” What is most likely?
questions.explanation: Pulling during braking plus one hot wheel both point to a brake on that corner failing to release.

questions.question: “The battery is new, but it repeatedly goes flat and the charging warning appears while driving.” What should be tested?
answers: The charging system and its connections
questions.explanation: A new battery going flat with a charging warning suggests it is not being recharged correctly.

questions.question: “The vibration follows road speed, not engine speed, and remains when coasting.” Which area fits best?
questions.explanation: A vibration tied to road speed and present while coasting points away from engine combustion and toward rotating road-speed components.

questions.question: “There is a clunk when changing from acceleration to deceleration.” What is a sensible first area to inspect?
questions.explanation: Load reversal can expose free play in drivetrain mounts, joints or related components.

questions.question: “An engine/emissions warning appeared soon after refuelling, but the car drives normally.” What simple item is worth checking first?
answers: The fuel-filler cap or seal is correctly secured
questions.explanation: A loose or incorrectly sealed fuel-filler cap can trigger an emissions-system warning on many vehicles.

questions.question: “A grinding noise began suddenly from one wheel.” What is the safest response?
questions.explanation: Sudden wheel-area grinding can indicate a serious brake, bearing or contact fault and should not be ignored.

questions.question: An engine cranks, has fuel pressure, but has no spark on any cylinder. Which system should be investigated next?

visual.ariaLabel: Engine cranks, fuel pressure present, no spark

answers: Ignition control and its power or timing inputs
questions.explanation: Cranking and fuel pressure remove two basic causes; no spark across all cylinders directs diagnosis toward shared ignition control or inputs.

questions.question: The car pulls right while braking, and the right front wheel is much hotter than the left. What best explains both clues?

visual.ariaLabel: Car pulls right while braking and right front wheel is very hot

questions.explanation: A dragging right brake creates excess heat and stronger braking force on that side, explaining both symptoms.

questions.question: On a conventional 12-volt charging system, battery voltage is 12.5 V with the engine off and 12.0 V while running with the lights on. What is the best diagnosis?

visual.ariaLabel: Conventional 12-volt charging system: engine off 12.5 volts, engine running with lights 12.0 volts

answers: The charging system is not supplying enough voltage
questions.explanation: On a conventional 12-volt system, charging voltage should rise while the engine runs; a fall under load shows inadequate charging output or connection loss.

questions.question: The engine overheats only at idle, the radiator is unobstructed and the cooling fan never runs. What should be diagnosed first?

visual.ariaLabel: Engine cools at road speed, overheats at idle, cooling fan does not run

answers: The fan circuit, motor and control command
questions.explanation: Road airflow controls temperature, but idle overheating and a stationary commanded fan identify the fan circuit as the first diagnostic path.

questions.question: A vibration rises with road speed, remains while coasting and does not change when engine speed is raised in neutral. What is the best focus?

visual.ariaLabel: Vibration follows road speed, remains while coasting, unchanged by engine speed

answers: Wheels, tyres, bearings and driveline components
questions.explanation: All clues tie the vibration to road-speed components rather than the engine’s rotating or combustion speed.

questions.question: A vehicle is supported only by a lifting jack, and work is needed underneath. What is the correct response?
answers: Lower it and use correctly rated supports at specified points
Place loose blocks under one wheel
Ask someone to hold the jack
questions.explanation: A lifting jack alone is not a safe support for work underneath; correctly rated supports must be used at the vehicle’s specified points.
